# std.graph

Graphs: one stored representation and the algorithms over "what comes after v".  Vertices and edges are domains, so per-vertex data is `[V]T`, per-edge data is `[E]T`, and mixing the two does not type-check. An algorithm takes any `Next<V>`: a stored `Graph`, a `[V]List` of arcs, or any fn from a vertex to a `Seq` of arcs. An arc is anything with `.to`; what else it carries (`.w`, `.e`) decides which algorithms accept it:  bfs(g, from: [s]) dijkstra(g, from: [(s, 0)])                          # arcs carry w dijkstra(g.weighted(a => 2 * a.w), from: [(s, 0)])   # weights from a fn bfs(p => p.adj4.filter(q => grid[q] != '#'), from: [start]) bridges(g)                                           # arcs carry e  Customizing a graph is a lambda over `g.out(u)`; nothing is rebuilt. Unreachable is `None`. Whole-graph algorithms need `V: Domain`.

In prelude (no `use` needed): `Functional`, `Graph`, `Lit`, `Target`, `Tree`, `TwoSat`, `Visit`, `bfs`, `components`, `condense`, `dfs`, `dijkstra`, `floyd_warshall`, `kruskal`, `peel`, `reachable`, `scc`, `topo`.

## Types & Constants

- `type EdgeArc<V, E, R> = (to: V, e: E, ..R without (u, v))` — The arc a build stores by default: the target, the edge id, and every field of the edge record except `u` and `v`.
- `type Tree<V> = [0..V.len - 1](u: V, v: V)` — \(O(n)\) to read.
- `type SimpleGraph<V, E> = [E](u: V, v: V)` — \(O(m)\) to read.
- `type ConnectedGraph<V, E> = [E](u: V, v: V)` — \(O(n + m)\) to read (connectivity is validated).
- `type Dag<V, E> = [E](u: V, v: V)` — \(O(m)\) to read.
- `type Digraph<V, E> = [E](u: V, v: V)` — \(O(n + m)\) to read (acyclicity is validated).

## `trait Next<V>`

\(O(\deg u)\) per walk of `out(u)`.

## `trait Target<V>`

\(O(1)\).

## `trait Weighted<W>`

\(O(1)\).

## `trait Edged<E>`

\(O(1)\).

## `trait WeightedNext<V, W>`

A graph whose arcs carry weights: shortest paths, MST over arcs, DAG folds.

## `trait EdgedNext<V, E>`

A graph whose arcs carry edge ids: bridges, two-edge components, edge blocks.

## `struct Reweighted<V, E, A, W>(g: Graph<V, A>, f: A -> W)`

\(O(1)\) per arc read: `g.weighted(f)`, the arcs of `g` with `.w` read as `f(a)` (or `f(u, a)`), `.to` and `.e` passed through.

- `fn out(self, u: V) -> yields (to: V, e: E, w: W)` — \(O(1)\) per arc plus one call of `f`; The arcs out of `u` as `(to:, e:, w: f(a))`.

## `struct Graph<V: Domain, A: Target<V>>`

\(O(n + m)\) memory and build.

- `fn directed<E: Domain, R: (u: V, v: V, ..), B: Target<V>>(edges: [E]R, keep: EdgeArc<V, E, R> -> B = a => a) -> Graph<V, B>` — \(O(n + m)\) time and memory, plus `m` calls of `keep`; A graph with one arc `u -> v` per edge of `edges`, in compressed sparse rows.
- `fn undirected<E: Domain, R: (u: V, v: V, ..), B: Target<V>>(edges: [E]R, keep: EdgeArc<V, E, R> -> B = a => a) -> Graph<V, B>` — \(O(n + m)\) time and memory, plus `2m` calls of `keep`; A graph with two arcs per edge of `edges`, `u -> v` and `v -> u`, both carrying the same `e`.
- `fn of(arcs: Seq<(from: V, arc: A)>) -> Graph<V, A>` — \(O(n + m)\); A graph from `(from, arc)` pairs: `arc` is stored as one of `from`'s arcs.
- `fn at(self, u: V) -> lends Slice<A>` — \(O(1)\); `g[u]`: the arcs out of `u` as an `Indexed` view, without copying.
- `fn out(self, u: V) -> yields A` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per arc; The arcs out of `u`, lazily: the `Next` implementation.
- `fn matrix<W: Ord>(self) -> [V, V]?W where A: Weighted<W>` — \(O(n^2 + m)\) time, \(O(n^2)\) memory; The weight matrix: `d[u, v]` is the least `.w` over the arcs `u -> v`, `None` without one.
- `fn deg(self, u: V) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of arcs out of `u`.
- `fn next(self, u: V) -> yields V` — \(O(1)\) per vertex yielded; Where `u`'s arcs lead: `out(u)` mapped to `.to`, repeats kept.
- `fn only(self, keep: V -> Bool = v => true, from: V -> Bool = v => true) -> Only<V, Self>` — \(O(1)\) to make; `keep` and `from` run per arc walked; The induced view on the vertices `keep` accepts: arcs from or to a rejected vertex are skipped.
- `fn weighted<E, W>(self, f: A -> W) -> Reweighted<V, E, A, W> where A: Edged<E>` — \(O(1)\) to make; `f` runs on every arc read; The same graph with each arc's `.w` read as `f(a)`; `.to` and `.e` pass through, so it is a `WeightedNext` and stays `Edged`.
- `fn has(self, u: V, v: V) -> Bool` — \(O(\deg u)\); True when some arc `u -> v` exists.
- `fn lists(self) -> [V]List<V>` — \(O(n + m)\); The targets of every vertex as plain lists, `lists()[u] == next(u).collect()`: the shape `std.flow` matchings take.
- `fn hops(self) -> [V, V]Int` — \(O(n (n + m))\) time, \(O(n^2)\) memory; The fewest arcs between every ordered pair, by a BFS from each vertex; `0` on the diagonal.; traps: when some vertex cannot reach another
- `fn edges<E>(self) -> yields Edge<V, E> where A: Edged<E>` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per edge; Every edge once, as `Edge(e, u, v)`.
- `fn peel(self, ready: ?(V -> Bool) = None, on_remove: ?((V, A) -> ()) = None) -> List<V>` — \(O(n + m)\) plus the calls of `ready` and `on_remove`; `peel(g, ready:, on_remove:)` as a method; see the free `peel`.
- `fn transpose(self) -> Graph<V, A>` — \(O(n + m)\); Every arc `u -> a.to` reversed to `a.to -> u`, its other fields kept (`(..a, to: u)`).

## `struct Paths<V, W: Add, A>`

\(O(n)\) memory.

Fields: `order: List<V>`.

- `fn get(self, v: V) -> ?W` — \(O(1)\) dense, \(O(1)\) expected `hashed`; `p[v]`: the distance to `v`, or `None` if no source reaches it (or the search stopped at `until` first).
- `fn iter(self) -> yields (v: V, d: W)` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per item; The reached vertices with their distances, in settling order: `for (v, d) in bfs(g, from: [s])`.
- `fn tight<>(self, g: Next<V>) -> [V]List<A>` — \(O(n + m)\); The arcs on some shortest path: for each reached `u`, the arcs `a` of `g.out(u)` with `p[a.to] == p[u] + w(a)`, where `w(a)` is `a.w` for `Weighted` arcs and `1` otherwise.
- `fn reached(self, v: V) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Does some source reach `v`?
- `fn path(self, t: V) -> ?List<V>` — \(O(\text{path length})\); The vertices of one shortest path from a source to `t`, both included, or `None` if `t` is unreachable; `[t]` when `t` is a source.
- `fn arcs(self, t: V) -> ?List<A>` — \(O(\text{path length})\); The arcs of `path(t)`, in walking order: `[]` when `t` is a source, `None` if it is unreachable.

## `struct Walk<V, E>`

\(O(m)\) memory.

- `@get fn vertices(self) -> yields V` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per vertex; The vertices visited, `start` first, then each arc's `to`: `arcs.len + 1` of them.

## `struct Lit<X>(pub x: X, pub value: Bool)`

\(O(1)\).

- `@get fn flip(self) -> Lit<X>` — \(O(1)\); The opposite literal: `Lit(x, v).flip == Lit(x, not v)`.

## `struct TwoSat<X>`

A conjunction of two-literal clauses over the variables `X`.

- `fn new() -> TwoSat<X>` — \(O(\lvert X \rvert)\); An instance with no clauses over the variables of `X`; every assignment satisfies it.
- `fn add_or(mut self, a: Lit<X>, b: Lit<X>)` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Adds the clause "at least one of `a`, `b` holds".
- `fn must(mut self, a: Lit<X>)` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Adds the clause "`a` holds" (`add_or(a, a)`).
- `fn implies(mut self, a: Lit<X>, b: Lit<X>)` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Adds "if `a` holds then `b` holds" (`add_or(a.flip, b)`).
- `fn at_most_one(mut self, lits: List<Lit<X>>)` — \(O(k)\) amortized; Adds "at most one of `lits` holds".
- `fn add_xor(mut self, a: Lit<X>, b: Lit<X>)` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Adds "exactly one of `a`, `b` holds" (two clauses).
- `fn add_eq(mut self, a: Lit<X>, b: Lit<X>)` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Adds "`a` and `b` hold together or not at all" (two clauses).
- `fn solve(self) -> ?[X]Bool` — \(O(\lvert X \rvert + \mathit{clauses})\); An assignment satisfying every clause, or `None` if there is None.

## `enum Visit<V, A>: Enter(v: V, via: ?A), Exit(v: V, via: ?A), Again(from: V, via: A)`

\(O(1)\): one event of `dfs`, the same shape as `Rooted.tour` yields: `via` is the arc that discovered `v` (`None` for a source); `Again(from, via)` is an arc into a discovered vertex.

## `struct Complement<V, G>(missing: G)`

The complement of `missing` over a domain `V`: an arc `u -> v` for every `v != u` that `missing.out(u)` does not reach.

## `struct Functional<V>`

\(O(n)\) build: the functional graph `v -> next[v]` (every vertex one out-arc).

- `fn new(next: [V]V) -> Functional<V>` — \(O(n \log n)\); The functional graph `v -> next[v]` (every vertex has one out-arc), with its cycles, tails and binary-lifting tables built.
- `fn on_cycle(self, v: V) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Does `v` lie on a cycle?
- `fn root_of(self, v: V) -> V` — \(O(1)\); The first cycle vertex reached from `v` (`v` itself on a cycle): the root of the in-tree hanging off the cycle that holds `v`.
- `fn depth(self, v: V) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The steps from `v` to `root_of(v)`; `0` on a cycle.
- `fn cycle_len(self, v: V) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The length of the cycle `v` eventually reaches.
- `fn after(self, v: V, k: Int) -> V` — \(O(\log k)\); The vertex `k` steps after `v`, by binary lifting: `after(v, 0) == v`.; traps: when `k < 0`
- `fn jump_while(self, v: V, pred: V -> Bool) -> ?V` — \(O(\log n)\); The first vertex `u` on the walk from `v`, `v` included, with `pred(u)`, or `None` if None appears.
- `fn dist(self, a: V, b: V) -> ?Int` — \(O(\log n)\); The fewest steps from `a` to `b`, or `None` if the walk from `a` never reaches `b`; `dist(a, a) == Some(0)`.
- `fn cycles(self) -> List<List<V>>` — \(O(n)\); Every cycle once, each in walk order from its smallest vertex.

## `struct IncrementalBridges<V>`

\(O(\log n)\) amortized per edge: 2-edge-connectivity under edge insertions.

- `fn new() -> IncrementalBridges<V>` — \(O(n)\); No edges yet: every vertex alone.
- `fn add(mut self, u: V, v: V)` — \(O(\log n)\) amortized; Adds the undirected edge `u - v`.
- `fn two_edge_same(mut self, u: V, v: V) -> Bool` — \(O(\alpha)\); Are `u` and `v` joined by two edge-disjoint paths?
- `fn same(mut self, u: V, v: V) -> Bool` — \(O(\alpha)\); Are `u` and `v` connected?

## `struct Edge<V, E>(pub e: E, pub u: V, pub v: V)`

\(O(1)\): one edge of a `Graph`: its id and its ends (as built for a directed graph, first in `V` order for an undirected one).

## `struct Only<V, G>(g: G, keep: V -> Bool, from: V -> Bool)`

`g.only(keep)`; see `only`.

- `fn out(self, u: V) -> yields G.Arc` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per arc of `g` walked; The arcs out of `u` the view keeps: None when `u` is dropped, else those whose `to` is kept.
- `fn deg(self, u: V) -> Int` — O(deg u in `g`); The number of arcs out of `u` the view keeps.
- `fn transpose(self) -> Graph<V, G.Arc>` — \(O(n + m)\); The kept arcs reversed, built as a `Graph` (record arcs as `(..a, to: u)`, a plain vertex arc as `u`).

## Functions

- `fn arc_len<A>(a: A) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The length of arc `a` as every graph algorithm reads it: `a.w` for a [`Weighted`] arc, 1 otherwise.
- `fn peel<V, G: Next<V>>(g: G, ready: ?(V -> Bool) = None, on_remove: ?((V, G.Arc) -> ()) = None) -> List<V>` — \(O(n + m)\) plus the calls of `ready` and `on_remove`; Kahn's peeling: repeatedly removes a vertex with no arcs left coming in, and returns the vertices in removal order.
- `fn topo<V>(g: Next<V>) -> ?List<V>` — \(O(n + m)\); A topological order (every arc goes forward in it), or `None` if there is a directed cycle: a `peel` that removed every vertex.
- `fn scc<V>(g: Next<V>) -> (domain C, comp: [V]C)` — \(O(n + m)\); The strongly connected components, as a fresh domain `C` and each vertex's component.
- `fn directed_of_pairs<V>(edges: List<(V, V)>) -> [V]List<V>` — \(O(n + m)\); `Graph.directed` on a plain list of `(u, v)` pairs: no edge domain, and each arc is the target vertex itself.
- `fn undirected_of_pairs<V>(edges: List<(V, V)>) -> [V]List<V>` — \(O(n + m)\); `Graph.undirected` on a plain list of `(u, v)` pairs: each pair gives arcs both ways, each arc the target vertex itself.
- `fn deg<V, A>(self: [V]List<A>, u: V) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of arcs out of `u` in an adjacency list, as `Graph.deg` is for a `Graph`.
- `fn next<V, A: Target<V>>(self: [V]List<A>, u: V) -> yields V` — \(O(1)\) per vertex yielded; Where `u`'s arcs lead in an adjacency list, as `Graph.next` is for a `Graph`: each entry's target, repeats kept.
- `fn has<V>(self: [V]List<V>, u: V, v: V) -> Bool` — \(O(\deg u)\); True when the adjacency list has an arc `u -> v`, as `Graph.has` is for a `Graph`.
- `fn transpose<V>(self: [V]List<V>) -> [V]List<V>` — \(O(n + m)\), a new adjacency list; The reverse of an adjacency list: `v` lists `u` once for each arc `u -> v`, `u` ascending.
- `fn components<V, G: Next<V>>(g: G) -> (domain C, comp: [V]C)` — \(O(n + m)\); The connected components of an undirected graph, as a fresh domain `C` and each vertex's component.
- `fn condense<V, C>(g: Next<V>, comp: [V]C) -> [C]List<(to: C)>` — \(O(n + m)\); The arcs between components: `out[comp[u]]` gets `(to: comp[a.to])` for every arc `a` of `u` that leaves its component.
- `fn two_edge_components<V, E>(g: EdgedNext<V, E>) -> (domain C, comp: [V]C)` — \(O(n + m)\), iterative Tarjan low-link; The two-edge-connected components (bridge blocks) of an undirected graph, as a fresh domain `C` and each vertex's component.; traps: in checked builds, when the graph is not undirected (an arc without its reverse on the same `e`)
- `fn cut_vertices<V, E>(g: EdgedNext<V, E>) -> [V]Bool` — \(O(n + m)\), iterative; Which vertices are cut vertices: removing one (and its arcs) leaves more components than before.; traps: in checked builds, when the graph is not undirected (an arc without its reverse on the same `e`)
- `fn two_color<V>(g: Next<V>) -> ?[V]Bool` — \(O(n + m)\); A 2-colouring of an undirected graph (no arc joins two vertices of one side), or `None` when an odd cycle exists.
- `fn bfs<V, G: Next<V>>(g: G, from: Seq<V>, until: ?V = None, enter: (V, Int) -> Bool = (v, d) => true, hashed: Bool = false) -> Paths<V, Int, G.Arc>` — \(O(n + m)\) dense; \(O(\mathit{reached} + \text{arcs scanned})\) expected `hashed`; Fewest arcs from any vertex of `from` to each vertex, by breadth-first search.
- `fn bfs01<V, G: WeightedNext<V, Int>>(g: G, from: Seq<V>, until: ?V = None, hashed: Bool = false) -> Paths<V, Int, G.Arc>` — \(O(n + m)\); Shortest distances when every weight is 0 or 1, from every vertex of `from` at distance 0: a deque, with 0-arcs pushed to the front.; traps: on an arc whose weight is not 0 or 1, when it is read
- `fn dijkstra<V, W, G: WeightedNext<V, W>>(g: G, from: Seq<(V, W)>, until: ?V = None, hashed: Bool = false) -> Paths<V, W, G.Arc>` — \(O((n + m) \log m)\); Shortest distances for non-negative weights, from `(vertex, starting distance)` pairs (a vertex given twice keeps the smaller start).; traps: on a negative weight, when it is read
- `fn fixed_cost_paths<S: Eq, M, W: Add + Ord>(from: List<S>, moves: List<M>, cost: M -> W, step: (M, S) -> ?S, until: ?S = None) -> Paths<S, W, M>` — \(O(\lvert S \rvert \lvert \mathit{moves} \rvert)\) time, \(O(\lvert S \rvert)\) memory; Shortest distances over a state space `S` whose moves have fixed non-negative costs, from every state of `from` at distance 0.; traps: on a negative cost
- `fn bellman_ford<V, W: Add + Ord, G: WeightedNext<V, W>>(g: G, from: Seq<(V, W)>) -> ?Paths<V, W, G.Arc>` — \(O(n m)\); Shortest distances with any weights, from `(vertex, starting distance)` pairs, or `None` when a source reaches a negative cycle (cycles no source reaches are ignored).
- `fn floyd_warshall<V, W, R>(mut d: [V, V]?W, over: R = Semiring(min, +)) -> Bool` — \(O(n^3)\) time, no extra memory; All-pairs shortest distances, in place: `d[u, v]` starts as the direct weight (`None`: no edge, usually from `g.matrix()`) and ends as the distance.
- `fn closure<V, W, R>(self: [V, V]?W, over: R = Semiring(min, +)) -> ?[V, V]?W` — \(O(n^3)\) time, \(O(n^2)\) memory; The value form of `floyd_warshall`, as `sorted` is to `sort`: a new matrix closed under `over:`, or `None` on a negative cycle.
- `fn find_cycle<V>(g: Next<V>) -> ?List<V>` — \(O(n + m)\); One directed cycle, as its vertices in walking order (each is followed by the next, and the last by the first), or `None` if the graph is acyclic.
- `fn bridges<V, E>(g: EdgedNext<V, E>) -> [E]Bool` — \(O(n + m)\); Which edges are bridges: removing one disconnects its ends.; traps: in checked builds, when the graph is not undirected (an arc without its reverse on the same `e`)
- `fn euler_walk<V, E>(edges: [E](u: V, v: V), directed: Bool) -> ?Walk<V, E>` — \(O(n + m)\); A walk that uses every edge exactly once (Hierholzer's algorithm), or `None` if there is None.; traps: when `edges` is empty and `V` is empty
- `fn dfs<V, G: Next<V>>(g: G, from: Seq<V>, seen: ?mut [V]Bool = None) -> yields Visit<V, G.Arc>` — \(O(n + m)\) total, \(O(1)\) per step; A depth-first walk from each vertex of `from` in turn, yielding `Enter(v, via:)` when `v` is discovered, `Again(from, via)` for an arc into an already discovered vertex, and `Exit(v, via:)` when `v` is finished.
- `fn reachable<V, G: Next<V>, S: Seq>(g: G, from: S) -> yields V` — \(O(n + m)\) total, \(O(1)\) per step; Every vertex reachable from `from`, each once, sources included.
- `fn dial<V, G: WeightedNext<V, Int>>(g: G, from: Seq<V>, max_w: Int, until: ?V = None) -> Paths<V, Int, G.Arc>` — \(O(n + m + \mathit{max\_w} + \mathit{d\_max})\); Shortest distances for integer weights in `0..=max_w` with a bucket queue (Dial), from every vertex of `from` at distance 0.; traps: on a weight outside `0..=max_w`, when it is read
- `fn johnson<V, W: Add + Sub>(g: WeightedNext<V, W>) -> ?[V, V]?W` — \(O(n m \log m)\); All-pairs shortest distances with negative arcs: one Bellman-Ford from a virtual source joined to every vertex, then a Dijkstra per vertex on the reweighted arcs.
- `fn k_shortest<V, W: Add>(g: WeightedNext<V, W>, from: Seq<V>, to: V, k: Int) -> List<W>` — \(O((n + m) \log n + k \log k)\); The lengths of the `k` shortest walks from any vertex of `from` to `to` (Eppstein).; traps: on a negative weight
- `fn negative_cycle<V, W: Add, G: WeightedNext<V, W>>(g: G) -> ?List<G.Arc>` — \(O(n m)\); Some cycle of negative total weight, as its arcs in walking order, or `None`.
- `fn min_mean_cycle<V>(g: WeightedNext<V, Int>) -> ?(sum: Int, len: Int)` — \(O(n m)\); The least mean weight over all directed cycles, as `(sum, len)` of a cycle achieving it (Karp), or `None` on an acyclic graph.
- `fn girth<V>(g: Next<V>, directed: Bool) -> ?Int` — \(O(n m)\), a BFS from every vertex; The length of a shortest cycle (the girth), or `None` if there is None.
- `fn smallest_topo<V>(g: Next<V>) -> ?List<V>` — \(O((n + m) \log n)\); The lexicographically smallest topological order (vertex order), by a min-heap instead of `topo`'s queue; `None` if there is a cycle.
- `fn dag_fold<V, T, M, G: Next<V>>(g: G, init: V -> T, step: (T, G.Arc) -> T, op: M) -> ?[V]T` — \(O(n + m)\); DP over a DAG in topological order.
- `fn count_paths<T: Add, V>(g: Next<V>, from: Seq<V>) -> ?[V]T` — \(O(n + m)\); The number of paths from a vertex of `from` to every `v` of a DAG, in `T` (a modular type keeps it exact).; traps: on overflow of `T`, as its arithmetic does
- `fn reach_sets<V>(g: Next<V>) -> [V]Bitset<V>` — \(O(n m / 64)\) time, \(O(n^2 / 64)\) memory; Reachability of every pair as bitset rows: `r[u].contains(v)` when some path of zero or more arcs leads from `u` to `v`, so every `u` reaches itself.
- `fn scc_times<V, E>(arcs: [E](u: V, v: V)) -> [E]?Int` — \(O(m \log m)\), divide and conquer over time; Offline incremental SCC: the arcs of `arcs` are added in order, and `t[e]` is the first index `i >= e` such that after adding arcs `0..=i` the ends of `e` share a strongly connected component, or `None` if they never do.
- `fn block_cut_tree<V>(g: Next<V>) -> (domain B, links: List<(b: B, v: V)>)` — \(O(n + m)\); The block-cut tree of an undirected simple graph: `B` numbers the blocks as the DFS (roots in vertex order, arcs in arc order) closes them, deepest first, as `blocks` does, and `links` joins each block to the cut vertices it contains.
- `fn blocks<V, E>(g: EdgedNext<V, E>) -> (domain B, block: [E]B)` — \(O(n + m)\); The biconnected block of every edge: edges, not vertices, are partitioned, so a cut vertex lies in several blocks and parallel edges share one.; traps: in checked builds, when the graph is not undirected (an arc without its reverse on the same `e`)
- `fn complement<V, G: Next<V>>(missing: G) -> Complement<V, G>` — \(O(1)\); The `Complement` of `missing`, as a view; see there.
- `fn odd_cycle<V>(g: Next<V>) -> ?List<V>` — \(O(n + m)\); An odd cycle witnessing that an undirected graph is not bipartite, or `None` when it is (exactly when `two_color` is `None`).
- `fn dominators<V>(g: Next<V>, root: V) -> [V]?V` — \(O((n + m) \alpha)\); The immediate dominator of every vertex reachable from `root` (Lengauer-Tarjan): the last vertex other than `v` that every path from `root` to `v` passes.
- `fn triangles<V: Ord>(g: Next<V>) -> yields (V, V, V)` — \(O(m \sqrt m)\) total, \(O(1)\) per item; Every triangle of an undirected simple graph once.
- `fn max_clique<V: Ord>(adj: [V]Bitset<V>) -> List<V>` — \(O(3^{n/3})\) worst case; A maximum clique of the undirected graph given as bitset rows (Bron-Kerbosch with pivoting); `n` up to about 64 in contests.
- `fn chromatic_number<V>(adj: [V]Bitset<V>) -> Int` — \(O(2^n n)\); The fewest colours such that no edge joins two vertices of one colour, by inclusion-exclusion over independent sets.
- `fn de_bruijn(k: Int, n: Int) -> List<Int>` — \(O(k^n)\); The de Bruijn sequence over `0..k` of order `n`: a cyclic sequence of length `k^n` in which every length-`n` word appears once.; traps: when `k < 1` or `n < 1`
- `fn kruskal<V, E, W, R: (u: V, v: V, w: W, ..), K: Ord>(edges: [E]R, by: R -> K = e => e.w) -> (total: W, take: [E]Bool)` — \(O(m \log m)\); A minimum spanning forest by Kruskal, as its total weight and the chosen edges.
- `fn prim<V, W>(w: [V, V]?W) -> ?(total: W, parent: [V]?V)` — \(O(n^2)\); A minimum spanning tree of the dense graph `w` (Prim without a heap), rooted at `V.first`; `None` if it is disconnected.
- `fn boruvka<V, C, W>(cheapest: ([V]Int) -> List<?(u: V, v: V, w: W)>) -> (total: W, edges: List<(u: V, v: V)>)` — \(O(\log n)\) rounds, each \(O(n)\) plus the call of `cheapest`; A minimum spanning forest by Boruvka rounds, for implicit complete graphs (xor MST, Manhattan MST).; traps: when `cheapest` returns a list whose length is not the number of components
- `fn arborescence<V, E, W: Add + Sub, R: (u: V, v: V, w: W, ..)>(edges: [E]R, root: V) -> ?(total: W, parent: [V]?E)` — \(O(m \log n)\); A minimum spanning arborescence rooted at `root` (Chu-Liu / Edmonds with a skew heap): `parent[v]` is the edge entering `v`, `None` at `root`.
- `fn spanning_forest<V, E>(g: EdgedNext<V, E>) -> [E]Bool` — \(O(n + m)\); A spanning forest of an undirected graph as chosen edges: a BFS from each unvisited vertex in vertex order takes the arc that discovers each vertex.
- `fn adjacency<V>(arcs: List<(u: V, v: V)>) -> [V]List<V>` — \(O(n + m)\); `directed_of_pairs` on named `(u, v)` arcs: neighbour lists indexed by vertex.
- `fn only<V, G: Next<V>>(self: G, keep: V -> Bool = v => true, from: V -> Bool = v => true) -> Only<V, G>` — \(O(1)\) to make; `keep` and `from` run per arc walked; The graph restricted to the vertices `keep` accepts: arcs from or to a dropped vertex are skipped as `out` walks.

## Example

```cp
domain V = 1..=3
let g = Graph.undirected([(V(1), V(2)), (V(2), V(3))])
let p = bfs(g, from: [V(1)])
print(p.dist[V(3)]!)
// output: 2
```
